Franzen
Man hospitalized with life-threatening injuries after critical incident in Wisconsin
By Indiana Schilz,
3 hours agoFRANZEN, Wis. (WFRV) – One person was hospitalized with life-threatening injuries Thursday after a critical incident in Wisconsin.
According to the Marathon County Sheriff’s Office, deputies were called shortly before 10:15 a.m. for a welfare check on an individual who reportedly made concerning statements of self-harm.
Wisconsin homicide: Daughter accused of beating her own mother to death with a rock
After several hours of search and coordination, deputies located the man shortly before 1:15 p.m. in the 182600 block of Comet Road in the Town of Franzen.
The individual armed himself with a knife during contact with law enforcement. Deputies used negotiation and less-than-lethal interventions to attempt to safely disarm him.
During the encounter, the man used the knife to harm himself. Deputies provided immediate life-saving measures, and he was transported to a local hospital, where he is receiving treatment for life-threatening injuries.
No deputies were injured, and authorities say the incident appears to be isolated.
Authorities renew call for information in 2020 Devil’s Lake murder case
Because use of force was involved, the Portage County Sheriff’s Office will lead an independent investigation, with assistance from the Wood County Sheriff’s Office, in accordance with Wisconsin law and policy.
Those experiencing a mental health crisis can call the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline or the North Central Health Care Crisis Center at (715) 845-4326 or 800-799-0122.
